Title: PC in VLAN 10 Cannot Ping Default Gateway
Symptom: Host PC-1 (192.168.10.50/24) cannot reach its default gateway 192.168.10.1 on Router R1. Link light on switch is amber.
Expected Fault: Switch port Fa0/1 is assigned to VLAN 1 (default) instead of VLAN 10.
Reviewer Notes: Diagnosis is accurate and evidence directly matches the show run output. Approved fix.

Title: Inter-VLAN Routing Fails on Router-on-a-Stick
Symptom: PC-1 (VLAN 10, 192.168.10.10) can ping its gateway 192.168.10.1, but cannot ping PC-2 (VLAN 20, 192.168.20.10).
Expected Fault: Parent physical interface GigabitEthernet0/0 on Router R1 is administratively down (shutdown).
Reviewer Notes: Classic subinterface prerequisite oversight. Verified parent interface must be brought up.

Title: Subnet Mask Mismatch Preventing Gateway Ping
Symptom: Host PC-3 (10.0.1.130) cannot ping default gateway 10.0.1.1 on Router R2. Neighbor PC-4 (10.0.1.50) has no issues.
Expected Fault: PC-3 is configured with a /25 mask (255.255.255.128). IP 10.0.1.130 falls in range 10.0.1.128-10.0.1.255, making gateway 10.0.1.1 appear off-subnet.
Reviewer Notes: Correct calculation of /25 boundary split. Verified.

Title: DHCP Scope Exhaustion in Office Subnet
Symptom: New laptop in Branch-1 gets APIPA address 169.254.x.x instead of receiving an IP from router DHCP server.
Expected Fault: The DHCP pool subnet is a /28 (16 addresses), only providing 13 usable client IPs. All 13 addresses are leased.
Reviewer Notes: Pool size expanded to /24. Clearing leases will allow laptop to acquire IP instantly.

Title: Extended ACL Blocking Web Traffic Due to Inverted Wildcard Mask
Symptom: Branch workstation PC-10 (172.16.10.25) cannot browse internal web server at 10.10.10.80 (HTTP port 80). Router drops packets.
Expected Fault: ACL 101 line 10 used a subnet mask (255.255.255.0) instead of an inverted wildcard mask (0.0.0.255).
Reviewer Notes: AI identified wildcard mask error correctly, but also forgot that DNS (UDP 53) and HTTPS (TCP 443) may be needed. Added permit for port 443 and domain.

Title: OSPF Neighbor Adjacency Down Due to Area ID Mismatch
Symptom: Routers R1 and R2 are directly connected on subnet 10.1.12.0/30 but cannot form OSPF adjacency. Routes are not exchanging.
Expected Fault: OSPF Area mismatch: R1 has link 10.1.12.0/30 in Area 0, while R2 has the same link in Area 1.
Reviewer Notes: Clear evidence in debug logs and running-config. Verified Area 0 alignment.

Title: Missing Default Route on Edge Router to ISP
Symptom: Internal hosts can communicate across all internal subnets but cannot reach public IPs like 8.8.8.8 or 1.1.1.1.
Expected Fault: Missing static default route (0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0) pointing to next-hop ISP gateway 203.0.113.1.
Reviewer Notes: Directly resolves the missing default route. Verified ISP next hop is reachable.

Title: NAT Inside Interface Configuration Missing
Symptom: LAN users cannot browse internet. Edge router has default route and ping to ISP succeeds from router, but client translation table remains empty.
Expected Fault: Interface GigabitEthernet0/0 is missing the command 'ip nat inside'.
Reviewer Notes: Verified. Inside interface was omitted during initial configuration.

Title: DNS Server IP Typo in DHCP Scope
Symptom: Clients can ping public IPs (e.g. 8.8.8.8) but cannot resolve domain names like www.cisco.com.
Expected Fault: DHCP scope hands out unreachable DNS server IP 192.168.1.254 instead of public DNS 8.8.8.8 or company DNS.
Reviewer Notes: Verified. Fixed DNS server parameter in DHCP pool.

Title: Trunk Port Native VLAN Mismatch Causing CDP Warnings & Traffic Leak
Symptom: Console displays '%CDP-4-NATIVE_VLAN_MISMATCH: Native VLAN mismatch discovered on GigabitEthernet0/1 (99), with Switch-2 GigabitEthernet0/1 (1)' repeatedly.
Expected Fault: Native VLAN mismatch across 802.1Q trunk: Switch-1 uses Native VLAN 99, while Switch-2 uses Native VLAN 1.
Reviewer Notes: Native VLAN must match on both ends of an 802.1Q trunk. Fix is 100% accurate.

Title: Guest Wi-Fi Can Access Secure Financial Server
Symptom: Guest SSID users on VLAN 40 (192.168.40.0/24) are able to ping and SSH into internal Financial Server at 10.50.1.10.
Expected Fault: Missing ACL on Guest VLAN 40 SVI or router interface to isolate guest traffic from internal RFC1918 private subnets.
Reviewer Notes: Comprehensive RFC1918 isolation rule with essential DHCP/DNS permits.

Title: DHCP Snooping Dropping Legitimate DHCP Offer Packets
Symptom: Clients on Switch SW-1 fail to receive DHCP leases after security hardening was enabled on the access switch.
Expected Fault: Uplink interface GigabitEthernet0/24 connecting to legitimate DHCP server is marked as untrusted under DHCP snooping.
Reviewer Notes: Verified. Uplink to authorized DHCP server must have 'ip dhcp snooping trust'.

Title: HSRP Active/Standby Virtual IP Mismatch
Symptom: Intermittent network dropouts; PCs occasionally lose default gateway connectivity when R1 primary goes down.
Expected Fault: HSRP Group 1 has conflicting virtual IPs: R1 is configured with 192.168.1.254 while R2 has 192.168.1.253.
Reviewer Notes: Spot-on diagnosis. Both routers were in Active state due to VIP mismatch.

Title: Static Route Pointing to Wrong Next-Hop IP
Symptom: Branch router R-Branch cannot route packets to Headquarters subnet 172.16.0.0/16.
Expected Fault: Static route next hop configured as 10.0.0.5 (out of local /30 subnet 10.0.0.0/30) instead of HQ interface 10.0.0.1.
Reviewer Notes: Accurate next-hop correction to 10.0.0.1.

Title: Missing 'ip helper-address' for Cross-Subnet DHCP
Symptom: Clients on VLAN 20 (192.168.20.0/24) fail to obtain IP addresses from centralized DHCP server located at 10.10.10.10.
Expected Fault: Router interface Gig0/0.20 lacks the 'ip helper-address 10.10.10.10' command needed to relay broadcast DHCP DISCOVER packets.
Reviewer Notes: Verified. Classic DHCP relay requirement across routed boundaries.

Title: Switchport Access Port Administratively Shutdown
Symptom: User plugged into wall jack connected to port Fa0/12 has no network link light and zero connectivity.
Expected Fault: Port Fa0/12 is administratively disabled ('shutdown').
Reviewer Notes: Simple shutdown port. Approved fix.

Title: VLAN Pruned from Trunk Port on Distribution Switch
Symptom: Users in VLAN 30 on Access Switch ASW-2 cannot reach any other network services; other VLANs on ASW-2 function normally.
Expected Fault: Trunk port Gi0/2 on DSW-1 explicitly allows only VLANs 10,20 ('switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20'), dropping VLAN 30 frames.
Reviewer Notes: Always use 'add' keyword so existing allowed VLANs are not overwritten. Fix confirmed.

Title: NAT Overload Access-List Missing Source Subnet
Symptom: Branch subnet 192.168.2.0/24 cannot access internet, while 192.168.1.0/24 has full internet connectivity through the same NAT gateway.
Expected Fault: Standard ACL 1 referenced by the NAT statement permits only 192.168.1.0/24 and does not include 192.168.2.0/24.
Reviewer Notes: Verified. Appending permit for second subnet restores NAT translation.

Title: Duplex Mismatch Causing Late Collisions and Extreme Latency
Symptom: File transfers between Server-1 and Switch SW1 are extremely slow with 40% packet loss and high latency.
Expected Fault: Duplex mismatch: SW1 Fa0/24 is operating at Half-duplex while Server-1 NIC is forced to Full-duplex.
Reviewer Notes: Matches textbook duplex mismatch signature: late collisions on half-duplex side + CRC errors.

Title: Standard ACL Applied Outbound on Wrong Router Interface
Symptom: Entire HR department (10.1.10.0/24) lost all internet and internal access after an administrator applied ACL 10 to block access to Server 10.1.50.5.
Expected Fault: Standard ACL 10 filters based on source IP. Applying 'deny 10.1.10.0' inbound on Gig0/0 drops all traffic originating from HR department.
Reviewer Notes: Standard ACLs should be placed close to destination, or use Extended ACL with specific destination IP.

Title: RIP Routing Protocol Version 1 / Version 2 Incompatibility
Symptom: R1 is sending RIP updates for subnets 192.168.10.0/28 and 192.168.10.16/28, but R2's routing table only shows classful summary or ignores routes.
Expected Fault: R2 is running default RIPv1 (classful, doesn't send subnet masks), whereas R1 is running RIPv2 with VLSM.
Reviewer Notes: Upgraded R2 to RIPv2 with auto-summary disabled for proper VLSM support.

Title: Switchport Security Err-Disable Due to MAC Violation
Symptom: Port Fa0/5 suddenly shut down when an employee swapped laptops. Interface status shows err-disabled.
Expected Fault: Port security violation: Hardcoded MAC address on Fa0/5 did not match new laptop MAC a483.e72b.4491, triggering port shutdown.
Reviewer Notes: Resetting the err-disabled state with sticky MAC configuration is standard practice.

Title: Static IP Gateway Set to Broadcast Address
Symptom: Static IP host 192.168.10.15/28 cannot reach any host outside local subnet.
Expected Fault: Default gateway is configured as 192.168.10.15, which is the directed broadcast address of subnet 192.168.10.0/28, rather than router IP 192.168.10.1.
Reviewer Notes: Verified broadcast address boundary check.

Title: OSPF Passive Interface Configured on Active Inter-Router Link
Symptom: R1 and R3 fail to establish OSPF adjacency across link Gig0/2 (10.1.13.0/30). Other OSPF neighbors on R1 work properly.
Expected Fault: Interface GigabitEthernet0/2 is configured as a passive-interface, suppressing OSPF Hello packet transmission.
Reviewer Notes: AI diagnosis correct. Added recommendation to follow best practice: 'passive-interface default' with explicit 'no passive-interface' for routed uplinks.

Title: Access VLAN Not Created in VLAN Database
Symptom: All ports assigned to VLAN 50 show inactive status, and devices in VLAN 50 cannot talk to each other or their gateway.
Expected Fault: VLAN 50 was assigned to access ports but was never created in the switch VLAN database ('vlan 50').
Reviewer Notes: Accurately caught 'Access Mode VLAN: (inactive)' condition.

Title: NAT Pool IP Address Conflict with Router Interface
Symptom: When NAT overload occurs, router console reports duplicate IP address conflicts and outbound TCP sessions drop randomly.
Expected Fault: NAT pool PUBLIC_POOL includes 203.0.113.1, which is already assigned to the router's physical interface Gig0/1.
Reviewer Notes: Fix excludes router interface IP from pool. Alternatively 'ip nat inside source list 1 interface Gi0/1 overload' can be used.

Title: Dynamic ARP Inspection (DAI) Dropping ARP Requests
Symptom: Static IP workstation PC-20 cannot ping its gateway or any peer on the switch; console logs DAI packet drops.
Expected Fault: Dynamic ARP Inspection (DAI) is enabled on VLAN 10 without an ARP Access List (ACL) to permit statically addressed hosts not found in the DHCP snooping database.
Reviewer Notes: Proper enterprise fix for static IPs under DAI using ARP ACL filter.

Title: OSPF MTU Mismatch Stuck in EXSTART/EXCHANGE State
Symptom: OSPF neighbor state between R1 and R2 stays stuck in EXSTART/EXCHANGE and never progresses to FULL.
Expected Fault: Interface MTU mismatch on the OSPF link (R1 MTU 1500 vs R2 MTU 1540), causing Database Description (DBD) packets to be rejected during EXSTART state.
Reviewer Notes: Standardizing MTU to 1500 allows DBD exchange to complete to FULL state.

Title: Subinterface Encapsulation Dot1Q VLAN Tag Typo
Symptom: Workstations in VLAN 100 cannot communicate with their default gateway 10.100.1.1 on Router R1.
Expected Fault: Router subinterface Gig0/0.100 is configured with 'encapsulation dot1Q 10' instead of dot1Q 100.
Reviewer Notes: Verified encapsulation tag typo fix.

Title: Wireless Guest SSID Mapped to Default Corporate VLAN 1
Symptom: Guest Wi-Fi visitors automatically receive IP addresses in the internal management subnet and can access core switches.
Expected Fault: The Guest WLAN profile is bound to the 'management' interface (VLAN 1) rather than the dedicated isolated 'Guest-VLAN' (VLAN 90).
Reviewer Notes: Critical security risk resolved by binding Guest WLAN to dedicated isolated VLAN 90 interface.

Title: IP Route Blackhole Due to Overlapping Summarization
Symptom: Server at 10.20.4.15 in Data Center is unreachable from Branch-A, while server 10.20.1.10 in the same DC works fine.
Expected Fault: Static route on R-WAN uses summary mask /22 (10.20.0.0 255.255.252.0), which only covers 10.20.0.0 through 10.20.3.255, omitting 10.20.4.0/24.
Reviewer Notes: Corrected summary mask from /22 to /21 (255.255.248.0) covering 10.20.0.0 - 10.20.7.255.

Title: DHCP Relay Helper Configured with Broadcast Instead of Unicast IP
Symptom: Branch PCs fail to get DHCP leases. Router CPU spikes intermittently.
Expected Fault: Interface Gig0/0 has 'ip helper-address 255.255.255.255' (local broadcast) instead of unicast IP of the centralized DHCP server 10.1.1.50.
Reviewer Notes: Verified. Helper address must point to unicast IP of remote DHCP server.
